chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

easyC.name: C major (Lauren's 'easy C' — 2-finger reduction)
easyC.note: Reduced 2-finger C voicing for confidence-building. Spelling verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js (2026-08-08) as C E G. 'Lauren's easy C' is a teaching label; arithmetic proves the fingering spells C major and is playable.

exercises.name: Make D
exercises.purpose: Land the D shape (top three strings only).

params.fingers: index(1) G 2nd, middle(2) high-e 3rd? NO — middle(2) on G 2nd? correct: index(1) G-string 2nd, middle(2) on high-e 3rd, ring(3) on B 3rd
params.open_strings: D and G strings ring open; low E and A muted

exercises.coaching: D uses the top three strings: index on the G string second fret, middle on the high e third, ring on the B third. Low E and A stay quiet. Bright, happy chord.

exercises.name: Four-change rotation
exercises.purpose: Cycle the change pairs with the metronome.

params.cue: one chord per 4 beats, change on the downbeat

exercises.coaching: Rotate: Em to C, Em to G, C to G, D to Em. One chord per four beats. The metronome keeps you honest. This is the muscle memory of changing.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: D is your last core open chord. With Em, C, and G you can play a huge chunk of popular music. Let's get D clean.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: D: index on G string second fret, middle on high e third, ring on B third. Low E and A stay quiet. Only the top three strings sound.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Now rotate the pairs — Em-C, Em-G, C-G, D-Em. One chord per four beats. The metronome exposes any pause. Smooth those out.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: Four chords, four change pairs. That rotation is the foundation every campfire song stands on.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: Core four done: Em, C, G, D. Lesson 8 adds A; Lesson 9 adds Am and you hit the "thousands of songs" set.
